title: L'Aire, Geneva
deck: What the pipeline does with three gauges on one river, a day at a time, before anything is mapped to XR.
steps: Hourly flow at each gauge and daily rain at its associated station, 2013 to 2025. The ribbon shows one column per week with the three gauges stacked on a shared spine; the Days view shows each day's mean flow with rain above.
Each day is summarised by seven numbers, measured against the gauge's own seasonal norm. Pick one to see it across the record.

An unsupervised model is fitted on 2014–2022 and scores every day, including 2023–2025, which it never saw. Colour runs from typical to most unusual; days below the training 90th percentile stay pale.
method: PCA with 3 components, one model per gauge, fitted on 2014–2022.
source: Office cantonal de l'eau, Geneva (OCEau): validated history export of the cantonal hydro-meteorological monitoring network.

groups.name: Bossenailles
groups.sub: hourly flow and daily rain, 2013–2025 · rain from David-Dufour
groups.note: 1.8% of this gauge's hourly flow readings are 0.01 m³/s or less (a few litres per second), in steps of about 0.004 m³/s, and some are 0.0. In log terms a move between such readings looks like a sudden jump of orders of magnitude, so near-dry days can score high without any storm. Read its highest scores as a possible effect of sensor resolution, not as verified events.

features.label: Flow vs seasonal norm
features.desc: log10 of the day's mean flow minus the median for that time of year: above or below normal.

features.label: Change since yesterday
features.desc: Change in log10 daily flow from the day before: rising or falling.

features.label: Peak-to-mean
features.desc: Highest hourly flow divided by the day's mean: how spiky the day was.

features.label: Largest hourly rise
features.desc: The biggest hour-to-hour rise in log10 flow within the day: how sudden.

features.label: Rain that day
features.desc: Rain at the associated station on the day.

features.label: Rain, three days
features.desc: Rain over the day and the two before.

features.label: Rain, week before
features.desc: Rain over the seven days before the day: how wet the ground already was.

limits: The model is fitted on 2014–2022 and scored on 2023–2025, years it never saw. The 2013 days are also scored, by inference. A day above the training 95th percentile is unusual compared with the days it learned from.
The record is about 12 years, so what counts as usual rests on a short history. Hourly flow is validated by OCEau; the validated archive ends on 31 December 2025.
The gauges are shown as Bossenailles, Centenaire, Pont-Rouge. Their order along the river is not confirmed with OCEau.
Nothing here has been tested with viewers. A high score means the day was unusual for this gauge, not that a person would feel it so.
